subject: Stock up on Maxwell House K-Cups on Amazon — 168 pods for just 39 cents each
posts:
Snag budget coffee pods on Amazon.
Evidence: Bulk discount, 30k reviews, inflationary backdrop
#Aletheia #Consumer #Economy

Buying in bulk on Amazon saves money on your daily coffee fix with highly rated Maxwell House K-Cups.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

While bulk deals offer short-term relief, coffee prices soared 34-46% recently and these pods rank low in taste tests.
Resulting Judgement: (-7.0, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
A commercial promotion masks severe underlying inflation and mediocre product quality behind a superficial bulk discount.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.5, z: 2)

- Fox News Deals: COND (0.0, 0.0) — Frames inflation-hit staples as consumer wins.
- Coffee Market Inflation: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — 34-46% price spikes in 2025.
Amazon shoppers can buy a 168-pack of Maxwell House medium roast K-Cups for $65.49, dropping the cost to about 39 cents per pod amid rising grocery costs.

The Bright Side:
Consumers get a slight bulk discount on daily caffeine needs.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a retail discount (WHAT) with systemic economic affordability (WHO/WHY).

Social Physics Analysis:
Retailers run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, packaging macroeconomic inflation as a clever consumer 'deal' to drive affiliate sales while deflecting attention from surging food costs.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Force imbalances favor commercial extraction over true consumer empowerment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Bulk discounts provide temporary relief from surging coffee prices.

The Unavoidable Lie: This retail deal proves that grocery inflation is beaten.

Alethekanon:
Packaging structural inflation as an exclusive shopping win is a masterclass in marketing sleight-of-hand. Real savings cannot outpace a 46% baseline price hike.

Awwthekanon:
It's tough out there when every cup of morning comfort costs more. We all just want a decent deal, but let's not pretend a price hike disguised as a discount solves the grocery squeeze.

Brothekanon:
Thirty cents a pod sounds nice until you remember coffee prices jumped nearly fifty percent last year. Buying in bulk is fine, but let's call it what it is.

Spirithekanon:
"Better is a handful of quietness than two hands full of toil and striving after the wind." Ecclesiastes 4:6 PASS
Chasing illusory bargains amidst rising costs only fuels endless striving.

Coffee costs can add up, but this Maxwell House K-Cup deal makes it easier to save. The two-pack includes 168 House Blend medium-roast pods and has dropped from $80 to $65 — just about 39 cents per pod.

READ MORE: October Prime Day is Tuesday — here's what's worth buying

This two-pack of coffee pods comes highly reviewed on Amazon. (Amazon)

Buying in bulk can help lower the cost of your daily coffee, and this two-pack brings each pod to about 39 cents. The 168 medium-roast Maxwell House pods have more than 30,000 Amazon reviews and a 4.7-star rating, making them a popular pick for budget-conscious coffee drinkers.

Made with 100% Arabica coffee, the House Blend offers a rich aroma and full-bodied flavor. The pods work with Keurig coffee makers, so you can brew a cup whenever you need it.

READ MORE: Amazon just dropped this $190 Keurig coffee maker to $100 — one of its lowest prices ever

More than 30,000 Amazon reviews praise the Maxwell House K-Cup's rich flavor, affordability and convenience.

One reviewer wrote: "This is the best bang for your buck! It's cheaper than the food store 95% of the time, and it's great for those who drink a lot of coffee. The flavor is always fresh."

"This coffee has become a dependable part of my daily routine. The medium roast strikes a nice balance, not too strong and not too mild, with a smooth flavor that's easy to enjoy," wrote another.

Another reviewer praised the convenience: "These K-Cups are some of my favorites. They taste great, are convenient and are compatible with Keurig machines. They are just right; very flavorful and not too bitter."

For more deals, visit www.foxnews.com/deals

The main drawback shoppers noted is that grounds can end up in the bottom of the coffee cup. You'll need to make sure your machine is cleaned properly before inserting pods, which can help mitigate this annoyance.

It's a fair trade-off, however, when you consider the price per pod. At $65, it's a solid choice for anyone who wants to save on their daily coffee fix and go for an affordable bulk option.
